rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
rules.description: Memory operations access outside the intended buffer boundary.
A read accesses memory before or beyond the valid buffer range.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
rules.description: Uncontrolled data that flows into decompression library APIs without checking the compression rate is dangerous
Checking for the "javascript:" URL scheme without also checking for "vbscript:" and "data:" suggests a logic error or even a security vulnerability.
User-controlled data that flows into decompression library APIs without checking the compression rate is dangerous
Arithmetic comparisons with NaN are useless: nothing is considered to be equal to NaN, not even NaN itself, and similarly nothing is considered greater or less than NaN.
Trying to invoke a value that is not a function will result in a runtime exception.
